On Tue, Oct 19, 2026 at 9:07 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you send a sizing sketch and a ballpark pricing table...

Claire — based on the numbers you gave, here’s a conservative starting sketch (first pass):

Baseline option (right‑size for 95th):
- Target 95th throughput: 450 req/s
- Avg tokens / request: 1.2k
- Concurrency target: 220 sessions
- Recommended pool: 12x A100‑class GPU equivalent (configured for mixed precision + quantized weights where appropriate)
- Expected steady throughput: ~480 req/s (headroom for headroom for model mix / scheduling)

Buffered option (burst credits + margin):
- Recommended pool: 15x A100‑class equivalent
- Includes 20% burst credit pool (credits consumed to exceed committed throughput for short windows)

Pricing (ballpark, monthly list / committed 12‑month):
- MSRP per A100‑equivalent GPU: $12,000/mo
- Baseline (12 GPUs): $144,000/mo list
- Buffered (15 GPUs): $180,000/mo list
- Volume tier discounts for 12mo commit: 10% @ annual commit >= $1.5M, 15% @ >= $3M, 20% negotiated strategic

Notes:
- Long context jobs (batch reports to 16k) are costlier per token; if these are >10% of workload we recommend isolating them to a smaller, provisioned model pool to avoid tail latency impact.
- We can enable prefix/KV caching for conversational flows to reduce per‑token cost on repeat interactions.

I attached a short proposal with a couple of model‑mix scenarios and estimated QPS per GPU. Also included workload-metrics.csv that maps your brief token distro to GPU CPU cycles.

— Ben

Hi Claire — I’m Logan on the accounts/finance side. Quick answers and a proposal for negotiation:  

1) Discounting: for a 12‑month committed spend around $1.6M we can do 12% off list (standard partner band). If you can move to a 24‑month commit or increase committed spend to $2.8M we can offer 18% — otherwise we’re open to a one‑time onboarding credit to offset first‑month cost.

2) SLA & throughput guarantees: we can contract a throughput SLO for the committed pool (e.g., sustained 95th at 450 req/s for baseline) with an automatic fallback policy to a compatible hosted model in rare capacity failures. 99.5% p95 latency per route is doable with the buffered plan and appropriate model‑mix constraints (we’ll codify model variants & routing in the SOW).

3) Burst credits / overage cap: burst credits are consumed from a pooled budget (minutes * extra QPS). Pricing model: pre‑bought burst credits priced at 30% of per‑token unit cost; overages beyond credits billed at 1.5x list, but we can cap overage billing at 25% above committed monthly cost with a soft cap if you take the buffered option.

4) Batch reports: recommended path is to schedule non‑urgent batches to off‑peak window and to provision a small lower‑priority pool for ad‑hoc urgent reports (we estimate 2–3 GPUs). This keeps tail latency from impacting interactive routes.

I’ve added Kimberly (Customer Success) to help scope the SOW and run a short pilot acceptance test with defined QoS metrics. If this aligns, Marissa — would you like me to produce a revised proposal with the 12% discount and an onboarding credit?

Thanks,
